Feature designs / Built-in browser / Tab and toolbar

Tab and toolbar

proposed not yet reviewed · design note README.md · spec 025 v0.11.0

Everything above the page and the page area’s own Erfana page, for spec 025’s browser tab: the editor tab, the navigation row with the origin field (the one place the true origin is shown), the reserved pick row, the find row, the strip rows this screen owns, and the empty tab. One static frame per state, drawn to scale with the system’s CSS. Build nothing from it until the owner approves it (025-FR-043).

How to read a frame. Every drawing is a picture (inert, aria-hidden); the caption names the surface and state, the spec ids, and – where the drawing follows an open decision the owner has answered – “Owner decision OD-n”; “Assumption” marks a placement no decision covers. Frames are macOS unless tagged Windows. The white page is third-party content (.ds-foreign-page), not Erfana. A menu or list that crosses into the page area is drawn over a still image of the page: it looks identical, and that is the point – the page keeps running underneath and nothing over it is the page’s.
Cards cited. New and proposed with this design: Origin field, Element picker (pick frame), Site prompts (pop-up row). Decided: Focus and keyboard, Menu, Form controls, Permission band, Rows and lists. Proposed: Tabs, Toolbar, Buttons, Tooltip, Badges, chips and keys, Feedback, Empty, loading and error states, Layering.

Browser tab (editor tab)

Tabs card markup and CSS. The browser tab is the second tab in each strip; the Markdown tab beside it shows the strip’s ordinary look. The full address is the tab’s description (tooltip and aria-describedby), never title. When the label is an address it is the origin display (Origin field card), never cut from its end.

Opening a browser tab – New browser tab and Open in browser tab

Two new controls (025-FR-001, 025-FR-010). New browser tab: an icon tool after the last tab in each editor strip, outside the tablist in the DOM; also in the palette and the app menu. Open in browser tab: a tool in the HTML preview bar, before Open in default browser.

Tab toolbar – navigation row

Back, Forward, Reload or Stop, the origin field, Open in system browser, DevTools, More – a role="group" named “Navigation”, every enabled control a Tab stop (note F-7). Same height as the HTML preview bar. Below it, the reserved pick row (OD-3).

Each control at rest, on hover and with keyboard focus

Buttons card states, at the tool height. Hover is a fill and the bright label; focus is the one ring, outward, offset 2px. The pressed Pick element is the fill plus the 2px lime foot – a shape, never colour alone. A disabled control is drawn in the frames above.

In a contrast theme the pressed Pick element takes the full Highlight treatment – fill, edge and HighlightText label (forced-color-adjust: none) – so on and off differ by more than one edge’s colour (M-33). The frame simulates the system colours; Windows High Contrast draws them for real.

Shortcut labels – macOS and Windows

Every caption renders through formatShortcut. One platform per frame; both drawn here.

Navigation and pick rows – full, compact, narrow and minimal tiers

The tab is a size container; each tier is a container query on its own width (thresholds in the header of browser.css, measured on these frames). Rows never wrap and never change height. The origin field is the last thing to shrink.

The longest host at every tier – the fold order

The worst string: committed address http://eu-west-2.preview.build-4812.cdn.staging.harbour-garden.co.uk:8080/reports/october with the “Not secure” badge, drawn at each tier’s lower bound and at the usual widths. Whatever the tier, room comes back in one fold order, each step only once the one before is exhausted: (1) the path, (2) whole subdomain labels from the front, (3) the zoom chip, Open in system browser and DevTools into More, (4) Forward and Reload into More, (5) the field’s margins shrink to 4px, (6) the badge word to its icon – “Not secure” kept as its name, (7) Back into More, last. More never shrinks and is never clipped. Scheme, registrable domain and port are whole in every frame.

Pick-row status slot – one line at every width

The slot is one tool high and never wraps a sentence: each part is nowrap, and a part that does not fit beside the ones before it leaves whole (it drops to a clipped second line). “Picking – Esc to stop” always stays, and the optional controls give way to it. Text is --text-base. The separator is drawn by CSS with equal space each side.

Origin field (address bar)

The new Origin field card. Registrable domain in --color-text-emphasis; subdomain labels, scheme, port and path in tertiary, so the domain is the one bright run. Elision: the path from its end, then whole subdomain labels from the front – never inside the registrable domain.

Suggestions under the address field

A listbox under the field; focus stays in the field (combobox, aria-activedescendant), so the active row draws the ring itself, inset. At most 8 history rows, address only – never a stored title. Nothing is asked of a remote service before Enter.

Inline message for refused addresses

The first strip row, as a Feedback band (error), linked to the field by aria-describedby. Red edge, error icon in the field, the typed text kept. Cleared on the next edit. The page under it is untouched.

Find-in-page bar

A row under the pick row while find is open (Chromium’s native findInPage paints the matches, so no match colour is drawn here). The count is a polite status, announced on change, not per keystroke.

Zoom chip

An action chip at the end of the field (Badges card), shown only when zoom is not 100%. Activating it resets to 100%. Name starts with the visible text (SC 2.5.3).

Pop-up-blocked control

A strip row on the first block (Site prompts card) and a chip in the field that brings it back. The row never takes focus; its buttons are secondary, so no answer is nudged.

The badge as its icon (fold step 6)

Drawn at 360px with fold steps 1–5 really done: path, subdomain labels, the zoom chip with Open and DevTools, Forward and Reload, the field’s margins. Then the badge word collapses to its icon; the word stays as its accessible name and the full deck description stays its accessible description. The remote-http glyph is circle-alert – it cannot read as a lock, and its round shape differs from the certificate triangle. Badge tooltip position, one rule (R6-M1): it stays inside the pick row’s band – never over the editor tab strip, the live page, the field, More, the banner’s first clause or the target button. Out of pick mode it starts under the badge; in pick mode it starts after “Picking – …”. It always ends before the target. At most two lines: when the full description does not fit, it shows the short form (deck row “Badge tooltip – short”); when even that does not fit, it does not show. In a pop-up window it opens in the origin strip’s band after the address, short form only. Shown on hover, and while the address bar has keyboard focus and the badge is icon-only; Esc hides it (rules in browser.css and on the Tooltip card).

Certificate warning sign

The same badge segment as “Not secure” on http, with the warning triangle in --color-error; its description says which failure.

Width presets

A menu button in the pick row, not a segmented control (three cells do not fit at 400px). Narrower than the panel: the page is centred with the frame hugging it. Wider: the area scrolls sideways under an Erfana scrollbar. Changing a preset resets zoom to 100%.

Target chooser

A menu button at the end of the pick row: where a send goes, before any send (Security rule 11). The terminal name truncates first; the process is never cut.

Empty-tab hint

An Erfana page in the page area (States card, first run). The field has focus. Lists are one Tab stop each with ↑ ↓ Home End and Enter (Rows card); sections with no rows are not drawn.

Exceptions

Where this screen departs from a card, with the reason. Each row is mirrored on the owning card’s Exceptions, naming this file; none is adopted until the owner approves the design.

CardThe cardThis screen, and why
ToolbarRows on --color-bg-secondary at the toolbar’s height.The navigation, pick and find rows copy the HTML preview bar (Permission band, decided): --color-bg-primary, 28px tools in --space-3 padding, so the two web-page surfaces in Erfana look alike; tools sit --space-2 (4px) apart so an outward ring never lands on the next tool (M-37). Proposed: --toolbar-tool-height on the Toolbar card instead of the local height override.
TooltipOpens above its trigger, lines wrap at 32ch.The editor tab’s tooltip opens beside the tab, inside the strip, with two one-line lines (address, then “Title:”), so a page-supplied title never covers the origin field or a focused row (H-02).
TooltipOpens above its trigger.The Pick element tooltip opens inside the pick row’s band, beside the toggle and after the banner’s first clause in pick mode (R2-H5, R3-M1).
TooltipOpens above its trigger, on hover or keyboard focus of the trigger, lines wrap at 32ch.The address bar’s Badge tooltip stays inside the pick row’s band: never over the editor tab strip, the live page, the field, More, the banner’s first clause or the target. Out of pick mode it starts under the badge; in pick mode after “Picking – …”; it always ends before the target. Two lines at most, with a short form when the full description does not fit; the box is capped at the pick row’s full height with 2px block padding and --leading-tight, so two lines survive raised text spacing. Pop-up window (no pick row): it opens inside the pop-up origin strip’s band, beside the badge after the address, short form only. When the band has no room – in a pop-up, or in pick mode at the narrowest widths (OD-16) – it does not show; the word or accessible description carries the state. It also shows while the address bar has keyboard focus and the badge is icon-only (the badge segment cannot take focus). Esc while it shows because the field has keyboard focus: the first press hides it and is consumed (focus and field unchanged), the next does the field’s Esc, and it stays hidden until the field loses and regains focus. Esc while it shows on hover with focus elsewhere: the press does that state’s routing action and hides the tooltip in the same press; it stays hidden until the pointer leaves the badge and re-enters. (R5-M7, R6-M1, R7-M1, R7-M4, R7-M5).
ButtonsThe busy ring is .erf-button[aria-busy]::before only.The tab’s loading spinner is a tab, not a button: it draws the same ring with button.css’s erf-button-spin keyframes until a shared spinner primitive exists. Also proposed: the full Highlight treatment for a pressed toggle in forced colours (M-33).
Badges, chips and keysAction chip ring outward, offset 2px.Inside the origin field the chip’s ring is the Focus card’s inset form, so it stays inside the field’s edge and the field draws no second ring (M-32).
